sjohn: St John's Co-Cathedral and the Caravaggio

The church of the Knights of Malta, austere outside and all gold inside: a floor of inlaid marble tombstones and a vault painted by Mattia Preti. In the oratory hangs Caravaggio's "Beheading of St John the Baptist", the only painting the artist signed.
palace: The palace that was the residence of the Grand Masters and is now the seat of the President of Malta. You visit the State Rooms with tapestries and frescoes, and the Armoury, one of Europe's largest collections of armour.
manoel: One of Europe's oldest working theatres, built in 1731: an all-gold Baroque auditorium with three tiers of painted boxes. You see it on a short guided tour.
barrakka: Upper Barrakka Gardens and the Saluting Battery
The terraced garden on the walls, with the best view of the Grand Harbour and the Three Cities opposite. Below, the gun battery fires twice a day: at noon and at 4pm.
lascaris: The tunnels dug under the walls, used by the British as a command centre in the Second World War: from here the defence of the island and the 1943 invasion of Sicily were directed. You see the operations room and the original maps.
elmo: Fort St Elmo and the National War Museum

The fort at the tip of the peninsula, where the Great Siege began in 1565. Inside, the museum tells Malta's military history, with aircraft, vehicles and Second World War memorabilia, including the Gloster Gladiator and Eisenhower's jeep.
gate: City Gate, Parliament and Republic Street

The city's modern entrance: the gate, Renzo Piano's Parliament with its façade carved like a quarry, the ruins of the old Opera House and the Triton Fountain. From here Republic Street, the main street, runs straight to the fort.
strait: Strait Street and the lanes of the centre

The narrow street parallel to Republic Street that for decades was the sailors' quarter: bars, music and nightclubs. Today it's full of bars, restaurants and craft workshops. The streets sloping down to the harbour have sea views at every crossing.
hastings: Hastings Gardens and the Marsamxett bastions
The garden on the bastion on the opposite side of the city from the Grand Harbour: from here you see Sliema, Manoel Island and Marsamxett Harbour.
birgu: The Knights' fortified town across the harbour, older than Valletta: narrow lanes, a marina full of yachts and the view of Valletta from the water. Ten minutes away by ferry.
